questions: What does "some case" mean precisely — any single consistent case shared by all keys, or literally any casing at all?
If all keys are already lowercase, does the "some case" branch make the "lower case" branch redundant, or are they mutually exclusive?
Should uppercase-only keys satisfy the "some case" condition even though they don't satisfy "lower case"?
How should mixed-case keys (neither strictly lower nor one consistent case) be classified?
Are keys with no cased characters (e.g. numeric strings) considered to satisfy either condition trivially?
Is "some case" meant to include the possibility of all keys being uppercase, or any arbitrary matching case?
Should a dictionary where keys are of two different consistent cases (some upper, some lower) return False?
Does the empty-dictionary rule (return False) override any of these case considerations?
